claims_about_writeup.quote: contribution.md (291 words: the self-authored contrast, the fit-split dose curve, the L25 boundary and handoff equivalence, prefix-over-read dominance, with citations)
claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up does contain roughly this word count and does cover the self-authored 70-pair contrast, the dose-7 peak with pass@10/log-rank numbers, the L25-30 inert boundary and the single-layer-24 near-equivalence, the prefix-vs-read dominance comparison, and ends with citations to Raman et al. 2026 and Okafor et al. 2026.

message_source_quote: Raman et al. 2026 (White-Bear Steering) is this exact setup (same model, lens, read layers, baseline) — a *stance* direction (think vs don't-think, concept and carrier matched within pairs) added in the pre-readout layers at a large dose makes the latent concept decodable. Since the rules forbid reproducing an existing method, I built my own instantiation around it.
writeup_source_quote: This builds on white-bear steering (Raman et al. 2026) and J-lens crowding (Okafor et al. 2026).

differences.what: The write-up also explicitly credits a second source, Okafor et al. 2026, for the J-lens crowding diagnosis that motivates the whole approach, while the message presents this crowding diagnosis (continuation-prior tokens outranking targets) as its own finding without naming or citing that paper.
differences.message_quote: A zero-vector probe of the metric server returned `examples` with top-10 readouts: the plain J-lens at L26/28/30 is crowded by sentence-initial continuation-prior tokens ("The", "At", "But", "When"…), with targets sitting at ranks ~27–72 behind them.
differences.writeup_quote: This builds on white-bear steering (Raman et al. 2026) and J-lens crowding (Okafor et al. 2026).

differences.what: The message is more explicit than the write-up about how closely the method's setup overlaps with Raman et al. 2026 (same model, lens, read layers, baseline, and the same think/don't-think stance-direction mechanism), whereas the write-up frames novelty mainly against 'the reading list' in general without spelling out this specific overlap with Raman's setup.
differences.message_quote: is this exact setup (same model, lens, read layers, baseline)
differences.writeup_quote: New in this submission, against the reading list: (i) the effect does not depend on the directed-modulation bank - it reproduces from fully self-authored prompts

rationale: Both documents credit Raman et al. 2026 (white-bear steering) as the basis the method builds on and state the novelty lies in using self-authored prompts, a dose-7 peak, an inert L25-30 band, and prefix-over-read dominance; the write-up additionally credits a second source, Okafor et al. 2026, for the J-lens crowding phenomenon, which the message omits by presenting that diagnosis as its own probe finding, while the message in turn states more plainly than the write-up how exactly the setup overlaps with Raman's (same model/lens/layers/baseline).
